units.function: Plugin database namespace and migration service with regex-based SQL policy, checksum ledger, advisory locking and restricted runtime query/execute facades over the shared database client.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends directly on filesystem SQL, Drizzle raw SQL, central plugin/migration tables and the plugin manifest's database declaration; worker host services call the runtime methods.
units.keyDataModels: Derived schema namespace, coreReadTables allowlist, migration key/checksum/version/status/error and parameterized runtime SQL/result rows.
units.lifecycle: Creates a schema, records its namespace, locks by plugin, validates and applies sorted SQL files transactionally, rejects checksum mutation, then validates and executes worker SQL through the server database role.
units.testAssessment: Nine pure SQL/environment cases passed and eight embedded-database cases skipped. Positive transaction/checksum tests are valuable, but the suite lacks an adversarial SQL corpus, database-role/RLS proof, tenant predicate enforcement, resource limits, symlink and migration-order attacks.
units.designRationale: Give plugins useful relational storage and controlled core joins without granting unrestricted public-schema writes, while keeping migrations idempotent and serialized.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs Connector data storage isolated by installation and company, with database-enforced least privilege, governed data-source contracts, bounded query execution and reversible/exportable lifecycle.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE deterministic namespace derivation, checksums, advisory locking and install-transaction rollback. Replace regex-only policy with parsed restricted queries or a typed data API plus separate least-privilege roles/RLS, mandatory company scope, budgets/cancellation and explicit migration/retention contracts.
units.responsibilityConflict: Unqualified relations and side-effectful SELECT functions can escape lexical checks; whitelisted public tables expose all companies without predicate enforcement; mutable manifests can broaden access; all SQL uses the shared server role and produces no per-query Responsibility/DataAuthorization evidence.
evidence: eb38b226 Fix LLM Wiki package and migration validation (#6010)

units.function: Pure SQL-policy/environment tests plus embedded-PostgreSQL namespace, migration, transaction, checksum and mutable-manifest activation scenarios.
units.dependencyDirection: Exercises production database service and loader against temporary packages and optionally real PostgreSQL, including bundled LLM Wiki migrations.
units.keyDataModels: Manifest database declaration, namespace and migration ledger, companies/issues, runtime rows and environment-driver worker env.
units.lifecycle: Validates statements, applies/reapplies/tampers migrations, installs with rollback, refreshes a disk manifest and queries or mutates namespace data.
units.testAssessment: Nine pure cases passed; eight database cases skipped. The test that refreshes a manifest intentionally adds capabilities, tools and broader coreReadTables without approval, providing direct evidence of a policy gap rather than a safety guarantee.
units.designRationale: Protect common namespace escapes and regress real migration packages while proving install rollback and checksum immutability.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS requires adversarial compatibility tests that prove both syntactic SQL restrictions and effective database privileges/data authorization under real tenant identities.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT checksum, idempotency, rollback and real-package fixtures; invert the mutable-refresh expectation and add parser fuzzing, RLS/role, company predicates, resource caps, cancellation, symlinks, ordering and retained-data tests.
units.responsibilityConflict: The suite explicitly codifies raw provider-key passthrough and unapproved capability/core-table expansion, while no accountable human, purpose, evidence or data-egress contract appears.
